# Gene paragraph drafts

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

All 1,305 entries remain drafts. Includes the original 1,133-gene roster and 172 hotspot supplement genes. See EVIDENCE-REVIEW.md and HOTSPOT-REVIEW.md for limitations.

## ABCB11

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ABCB11 encodes bile salt export pump. Annotated molecular activities include ATP hydrolysis activity and ABC-type xenobiotic transporter activity. It participates in cholesterol homeostasis and lipid homeostasis. ([NCBI Gene 8647](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/8647), [UniProt O95342](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/O95342/entry)). Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis type 2 (autosomal recessive). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). This gene is included in cancer-panel definitions, but a disease-specific somatic association has not been assigned from the alteration-context sources reviewed for this draft. ([glioma_dfci_2020_dfci_oncopanel3](https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/cBioPortal/datahub/master/reference_data/gene_panels/data_gene_panel_glioma_dfci_2020_dfci_oncopanel3.txt)).

## ABCC10

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ABCC10 is the approved symbol for ATP binding cassette subfamily C member 10. Reviewed functional annotations implicate its product in ABC-type glutathione S-conjugate transporter activity; ABC-type transporter activity; leukotriene metabolic process. ([NCBI Gene 89845](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/89845), [UniProt Q5T3U5](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q5T3U5/entry)). No conflict-free strong or definitive constitutional disease relationship met the source-selection criteria for this draft; this does not exclude a germline association. ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Cancer Hotspots v1 reports recurrent residue-level observations in Breast carcinoma; Glioblastoma; Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. This is statistical recurrence evidence; it does not establish that every variant in this gene is a driver or a clinically actionable alteration. Evidence in this collection is restricted to the historical V1 release. ([PMID 26619011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26619011/)).

## ABL1

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ABL1 encodes tyrosine-protein kinase ABL1. Annotated molecular activities include kinase activity and protein kinase activity. It participates in mismatch repair and intracellular signal transduction. ([NCBI Gene 25](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/25), [UniProt P00519](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00519/entry)). Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to congenital heart defects and skeletal malformations syndrome (autosomal dominant). ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Reported somatic alteration contexts include Acute myeloid leukemia; Chronic myeloid leukemia; B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma. The alteration class and exact variant must be assessed in the disease context. ([Tumor Driver Atlas](https://mikexiong2.github.io/molecular-tumor-drivers/)).

## ABL2

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

ABL2 encodes tyrosine-protein kinase ABL2. Annotated molecular activities include protein kinase activity and protein tyrosine kinase activity. It participates in signal transduction and negative regulation of Rho protein signal transduction. ([NCBI Gene 27](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/27), [UniProt P42684](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P42684/entry)). No constitutional disease assertion was retrieved in the reviewed GenCC snapshot; this does not exclude a germline association. ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). ABL2 can participate in leukemia-associated rearrangements, including fusion with ETV6. Interpretation requires the actual fusion structure and disease context. ([NCBI Gene 27](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/27)).

## H3-3A

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

H3-3A encodes the histone variant H3.3, which is incorporated into chromatin independently of DNA replication and contributes to regulation of chromatin structure and transcription. ## H3-3B

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

H3-3B encodes the histone variant H3.3, which participates in replication-independent nucleosome assembly and regulation of chromatin organization. SRSF2 encodes a serine/arginine-rich RNA-binding splicing factor that regulates splice-site selection and processing of pre-mRNA. ([NCBI Gene 6427](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/6427)). No constitutional disease assertion was retrieved in the reviewed GenCC snapshot; this does not exclude a germline association. ([GenCC snapshot](https://thegencc.org/download)). Somatic SRSF2 mutations occur in myelodysplastic and myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasms. Disease classification requires the accompanying clinical, morphologic, and molecular findings. ([PMID 22389253](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22389253/)).

## TERC

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

TERC encodes the RNA component of telomerase, providing the template used by the TERT catalytic subunit to add telomeric repeats to chromosome ends. ([NCBI Gene 7012](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/7012)). Pathogenic constitutional TERC variants cause autosomal dominant telomere biology disorders, including dyskeratosis congenita. Marrow failure and myeloid malignancy risk occur within this inherited disease context; a tumor-only result does not establish constitutional origin. ([PMID 11574891](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11574891/), [ClinGen SGC-107615.2](https://search.clinicalgenome.org/kb/gene-validity/CGGV:assertion_cfdf86d0-9441-40bf-a1da-ab2c85f775cd-2024-11-25T17:00:00.000Z)). Somatic copy-number gain involving the TERC region has been associated with progression of cervical neoplasia to invasive carcinoma. Regional gain is distinct from the constitutional loss-of-function mechanisms underlying telomere biology disorders. ([PMID 17054308](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17054308/)).

## TP53

Pathologist review needed — LLM-generated summary/review.

TP53 encodes the p53 transcription factor, a tumor suppressor that coordinates cellular stress responses through cell-cycle arrest, DNA repair, senescence, and apoptosis. ([NCBI Gene 7157](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/7157)). Germline pathogenic variants cause autosomal dominant Li-Fraumeni syndrome, which predisposes to a broad spectrum of cancers, notably early-onset breast cancer, sarcomas, central nervous system tumors, and adrenocortical carcinoma. ([GeneReviews: Li-Fraumeni Syndrome](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1311/)). Somatic TP53 mutations occur across many cancer types. The biological effect varies by alteration, and a tumor-detected TP53 variant alone does not establish a germline diagnosis. ([NCBI Gene 7157](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/7157), [GeneReviews: Li-Fraumeni Syndrome](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1311/)).
